analysis.title: GS SECTOR SPECIALISTS: Energy, Natural Resources and Utilities Preview: Tuesday Thoughts 10 Nov 2026
key_insights: Desk conversations describe a 'race to the bottom' on crude, with the risk premium in the barrel eroding and a clear distinction between freight constraints and supply constraints.

OXY is the last large-cap E&P to report this season. The desk says the topical E&P themes (cost inflation, potentially higher capex, ground game narratives, continued efficiency gains) were already covered by earlier reports, so little is left for the print itself.

OXY quarter: EPS and FCF beat the Street, and oil production came in ahead of the Street and above the midpoint of guidance. 4Q guidance is lighter on oil, and the desk expects more color on the call about which regions or assets drive the implied softness.
OXY updated STRATOS timing, capex and long-term offtakes. The desk says investors have not discussed STRATOS in recent months, so it expects views on the spend rather than the offtakes.

OXY set a new $6 bn debt milestone after reaching its $10 bn milestone. The desk calls this a positive, but notes bears will argue deleveraging is already known and there is no incremental update on the preferreds.
The OXY call today will focus on the 2027 capital program and early thoughts on volume guidance.

Gas: the desk describes the specialist view as 'the commodity is tough, but maybe the equities aren't.' Macro backdrop: oil continues to slide, gasoline is seasonally weaker, TTF depends on weather and Russia/Ukraine, and diesel is tight but known.

Questions on gas demand focus on how much is at risk if data center buildout does not materialize in key states or regions. With most dry gas names at the low end of their ranges and seasonality favorable, there is some willingness to buy.

The desk still sees longer-term interest in owning gas volumes over price. It notes the trade was or is crowded, gas pipeline stocks have moved more with the power trade and baskets, and there is less of a valuation call at this point.

Nuclear: the desk highlights comments from the CEG earnings call on 9 Nov. CEG management said customers are interested in existing nuclear, citing announced deals, and that new combined cycle gas plant cost estimates keep rising. CEG said its nuclear upgrade capital cost is not materially outside the range of current CCGT estimates, with little to no incremental fuel or operating maintenance costs.
